clue.text: Opener caught — hubbub at the Tavern?

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a row is a noisy commotion or din
a tavern is a pub, and a pub's drinking room is a bar

explanation.surface: A cricket opener is dismissed amid the noise at the Tavern, a well-known bar beside Lord's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' tempts as a batsman with 'caught' following, but it defines a tool for prising things open.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is a lever used to prise open boxes and doors, hence a tool that opens.

clue.text: Secure report of a congregation that's little more than gross?

annotationWithheld.why: Secure report of a congregation that's little more than gross? (6): CL (150, a little over a gross of 144) + INCH (little) is the likely build, but no parse accounts for 'report of' and no blog was found to confirm it
annotationWithheld.clue: Secure report of a congregation that's little more than gross?

clue.text: Town's ancient guy who must have been out of the ark

parts.note: ancient means old

parts.words: guy who must have been out of the ark
parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's sons, who sailed in the ark and so came out of it

explanation.surface: A town's oldest resident is mocked as antediluvian, as if he had stepped off Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the ark' is the idiom for old-fashioned, but here it is literal: Ham left the ark with his father Noah. OLDHAM is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a large town in Greater Manchester, England.

clue.text: Beastly male commanded individual to work hard

parts.note: a buck is the male of animals such as deer or rabbits
led means commanded or directed
own means individual or particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A domineering male animal orders one of the herd to get on with the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle down is an idiom meaning to apply oneself seriously to a task.

clue.text: Counter providing limited supply of Devonshire butter

indicators.note: only a small portion of the words Devonshire butter is taken, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A grocer's counter offers only a small ration of the West Country's butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter in the surface but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to counter an argument by offering opposing evidence.

clue.text: Disagreeable resting place for creature at sea?

parts.note: a crab is a sea creature
a bed is somewhere to rest

explanation.surface: A grumpy question about where a sea creature lies down for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order; 'for' just joins them as a bed belonging to a crab.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabbed means bad-tempered or irritable, so a crabbed person is disagreeable.

clue.text: Dress requiring cash — men go wild

indicators.note: wild suggests something running out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An expensive gown costs money, and the men go crazy over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wild' reads as a phrase, but 'go' is fodder and 'wild' alone rearranges CASH MEN GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a straight, close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar.

clue.text: A pitch full of grey dust?

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, and a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A sports pitch is covered in grey powdery dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a playing field, but it means a throw: a shy, as at a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means covered with or resembling ash, the grey powder left by burning.

clue.text: Something pointed — I am able to provide a defence

parts.note: a barb is a sharp backward-pointing spike, as on a fish-hook
I am able means I can

explanation.surface: Someone with a sharp weapon boasts that they can protect themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbican is a fortified outer gateway or tower guarding a castle or city, a defensive work.

clue.text: D-day's arranged without a particular fighting force — bunch little good against Hitler!

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the anagram goes around the other letters
arranged means the letters of D-day's are set out in a different order

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines, a specific British fighting force

explanation.surface: A rearranged D-Day force is mocked as a gang that would have been little use against Hitler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: the rearranged letters wrap around A and the marines. DAD'S ARMY is a classic British TV comedy about the wartime Home Guard, a bunch of elderly volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom's Home Guard platoon of old men was a comic band unlikely to stop a German invasion.

clue.text: Half a signal from the subcontinent

indicators.note: half means only the front part of the word for a signal is kept

parts.note: an indicator is a signal, such as a car's flashing light

explanation.surface: Only half of a message gets through from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' is loose: five of the nine letters are kept, the front portion of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is an adjective for things of the Indian subcontinent, especially its languages.

clue.text: Ran around to that place and chatted

indicators.note: around means the word for ran is placed on both sides of the other piece

parts.note: colours that run are said to bleed, so ran means bled
there means to that place

explanation.surface: Someone jogged over to a spot and then gossiped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' suggests running, but it is dye running: BLED. To blether is to talk at length foolishly, a Scottish and northern word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blethered means talked idly or foolishly at length, so it is a synonym for chatted.

clue.text: Fakes a healthy looking colour to get hugged by boy leaving Spain

indicators.note: to be hugged by something is to be held inside it, so one piece goes within the other
leaving signals that a letter departs from the boy's name

parts.note: Charles is a boy's name
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
a tan is a suntan, often thought to look healthy

explanation.surface: Impostors with a fake glow are embraced by a lad who has left Spain behind.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARLES loses E to give CHARLS, which hugs A TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlatans are people who falsely claim skill or knowledge, so they are fakes.

clue.text: Capital city a short distance to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a mil is a thousandth of an inch, a very short distance

explanation.surface: A capital lies just a little way to the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Single papa in difficulty? Offer some tips maybe

indicators.note: being in difficulty means being in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A struggling single father gets some advice to help him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice, but here it means gratuities. LAGNIAPPE is a word from Louisiana for a small bonus gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagniappes are small extra gifts given to a customer, of which gratuities are a kind.

clue.text: Foreign city ventures sadly suffering a setback in the morning

parts.note: to venture is to dare, so ventures means dares

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, meaning sadly
AM is short for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Ventures in a distant city sadly go wrong early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: ALAS reversed gives SALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the largest city of Tanzania, in East Africa.

clue.text: Once again devises outlet with external controls

indicators.note: having something external means it is wrapped around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: reins are the straps used to control a horse, hence controls in general
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: A shop is redesigned again, with its controls outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent is to devise something anew, so reinvents means once again devises.

clue.text: Man's trapped bird in high water barrier

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Adam was the first man, and the 's stands for has
a swan is a large water bird

explanation.surface: A man has caught a bird beside a towering dam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aswan High Dam is the huge dam on the Nile in Egypt, so 'high' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam holds back the Nile in Egypt, its later structure known as the High Dam.

clue.text: Clean out container on top — it's got a needle in it

definitions.text: it's got a needle in it

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on top means coming first

parts.note: a bin is a container

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters of Clean are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tidies out a container placed on top of a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' rearranges CLEAN to NACLE, set below BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A binnacle is the housing on a ship's deck holding the compass, whose needle points north.

clue.text: Singer offering endless yuck, Western guy embracing chart success

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: slime is something sticky that makes you say yuck

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
a guy is a man
a hit is a record that does well in the charts

explanation.surface: A singer offers revolting slime while a cowboy celebrates a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yuck' is a cry of disgust standing for its cause. SLIM WHITMAN was an American country singer famous for yodelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim Whitman was an American country and western vocalist with several UK hits.

clue.text: Pine for a Latin book in the Catholic church

parts.note: to pine for someone is to miss them

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a Latin prayer book used at Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is a book containing the texts used for celebrating Mass through the year.

clue.text: Sort of cousin with name inscribed in stone

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside, so the letter sits within the stone

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: A family member's name is carved in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a relative descended through the male line, a kind of kinship that can include cousins.

clue.text: Female friend from Somerset town shedding many pounds externally

indicators.note: shedding means losing letters from the town's name
externally means the lost letters come from the outside of the word, at both ends

parts.note: Taunton is the county town of Somerset, in south-west England
a ton is a unit of weight of many pounds

explanation.surface: A woman from a Somerset town is losing lots of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is split around the word: T at the front and ON at the end come off.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt is a familiar title for an older woman friend of the family, not only a relative.

clue.text: Leaving behind public, a ruler on the right

indicators.note: in an across entry, on the right means placed after

parts.note: overt means open and public
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch goes public by moving to the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaking means passing another vehicle, so leaving it behind.

clue.text: The man drinks something alcoholic? The opposite — something watery

indicators.note: drinks means taking in, so one word goes inside another
the opposite means the drinking is reversed, so the drink takes in the man

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man drinks spirits, or rather, a watery fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' reverses who drinks whom: the spirit takes in the man, not the man the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Traditional book for bringing English tot up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Bringing English to a small child to raise them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child, but it is a verb meaning add. ADD reversed gives DDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a traditional collection of Old Norse poems and myths.

clue.text: Undesirable feature of eg the Sixties once Love disappears?

parts.note: the Sixties is an example of a decade

indicators.note: disappears signals that a letter is taken out of once

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Moral decay marked the Sixties once free love had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' is itself fodder: it loses O to give NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral decline, an undesirable trait of a society or era.

clue.text: 8 providing a recipe for food

parts.note: 8 is the answer to 8 down, a sitcom title read here as Pa's TA, a dad's army
TA is the Territorial Army, an army of volunteers

explanation.surface: A sitcom title supplies the recipe for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is DAD'S ARMY; read literally, a dad's army is PA'S TA, TA being Britain's Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian food made from durum wheat dough.

clue.text: Female ravers send a man almost crazy

indicators.note: crazy suggests mixed up, so these letters go in a new order
almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Wild women drive a man nearly out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravers' sounds modern, but the maenads were frenzied female followers of Bacchus in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were women who raved in ecstatic frenzy during rites for the wine god.

clue.text: Wine stockist runs out — initially order put back

indicators.note: initially means placed at the start of the answer
put back means written backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: out means removed from the word

parts.note: a seller is someone who stocks and sells goods
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A wine merchant has run out of stock, so an order is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' places the turned honour at the front; 'out' is the deletion signal, with 'runs' the letter that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the Moselle valley in Germany and France.
